name: Blood Trails fires its Blood Trail proc from a periodic damage tick (#510)
contract: Blood Trails 804858 reads 'Periodic damage and healing now causes targets to spill a pool of blood beneath them.' Its single real effect is aura 42 (SPELL_AURA_PROC_TRIGGER_SPELL) on Blood Trail 804857, DBC ProcChance 100, but Spell.dbc gives 804858 ProcFlags 0 and no spell_proc row existed, so SpellMgr::LoadSpellProcs skipped the record entirely (Aura::GetProcEffectMask returns 0 without an entry) and 804857 could never fire. The new spell_proc row (ProcFlags 262144 = PROC_FLAG_DONE_PERIODIC, SpellTypeMask 3 = DAMAGE|HEAL, SpellPhaseMask 2 = PROC_SPELL_PHASE_HIT, Chance 0 deferring to the record's own ProcChance 100) makes the aura reachable. AuraEffect::HandlePeriodicDamageAurasTick and AuraEffect::HandlePeriodicHealAurasTick both assign procAttacker = PROC_FLAG_DONE_PERIODIC identically (SpellAuraEffects.cpp), so a single periodic-damage tick from Taldaram's Torment 800772 (SPELL_AURA_PERIODIC_DAMAGE, 3000 ms amplitude) is a sufficient, deterministic (100% chance) proof that the row reaches the engine's shared periodic-tick proc path; the periodic-heal half is not separately scenario-proven here since it shares the identical native flag.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
SETUP: Blood Trails is learned and self-applies
SETUP: the periodic damage effect is ticking on the target
Let the first 3000 ms damage tick land
DISCRIMINATING: the periodic damage tick procs Blood Trail
